evals.prompt: Read-only modeling: staff call an order confirmed when payment clears; the UI calls it confirmed when inventory is held. The supplied policy allows cancellation before payment clears. The current endpoint permits any UI-confirmed order. Clarify the domain for a cancellation change.
evals.expected_output: A scoped vocabulary and rule model showing the conflicting meanings and enforcement gap.
assertions: Keeps the staff and UI meanings distinct.
Uses the supplied payment boundary with allowed and rejected examples.
Separates current endpoint enforcement from agreed policy.
Invents no refund rules and makes no edits.

evals.prompt: Model only: a loan can be requested, approved, or disbursed. Policy says disbursement requires approval by a different employee from the requester. The code checks state but not employee identity. No redesign is authorized.
evals.expected_output: A bounded state/rule model with the separation invariant and missing enforcement.
assertions: Models requested to approved to disbursed using supplied states.
Names the different-employee invariant and its supplied source.
Identifies the identity-check gap without forcing a new architecture.
Does not implement or broaden the model to the whole lending business.

evals.prompt: Read-only: model the return eligibility rules. Note A says within 14 days of receipt; note B says within 30 days of purchase. Neither has approval status. The code uses 30 days. We need to know what must be settled before implementation.
evals.expected_output: Conflicting candidate rules, observed implementation, and a decision-changing unresolved boundary.
assertions: Does not declare the code or either note authoritative.
Explains differing time windows and start events.
Does not invent exceptions or change the system.

evals.prompt: Use model-domain to assess whether modeling is useful here: rename the already agreed UI label from Submitted to Sent. Its meaning and behavior are unchanged, and no domain rule is disputed.
evals.expected_output: A brief determination that no modeling exercise is needed for the settled label edit.
assertions: Preserves the requested label and meaning.
Does not invent a glossary, state model, or business policy exercise.
Does not expand the request to an architecture change.

evals.prompt: Read-only model: an agreed architecture decision says browser code must not import the payment provider module; only the payment service may use it. Domain rules say a payment has requested and settled states. A project dependency checker enforces the import rule, but its latest result is unavailable. Model only the relevant boundaries.
evals.expected_output: A scoped domain model with the agreed architectural boundary and a focused enforcement check remaining unverified.
assertions: Cites the supplied architecture constraint instead of inventing another.
Names the existing dependency checker as relevant evidence and does not claim it passed.
Distinguishes state rules, architectural boundary, and current enforcement proof.
Does not prescribe new governance or redesign the payment system.
